candidates.name: Myocardial Infarction
support_spans: ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF
thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery

candidates.why: The patient had ST-segment elevation and thrombotic occlusion of a coronary artery, which are diagnostic of myocardial infarction.

candidates.why: The patient's blood pressure dropped significantly, which is consistent with cardiogenic shock, a complication of myocardial infarction.

candidates.name: Acute Coronary Syndrome with Cardiogenic Shock
support_spans: sudden-onset chest pain
blood pressure fell to 60/40 mm Hg
ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF
contradict_spans: normal heart rate and blood pressure initially
candidates.why: The patient's presentation with sudden-onset chest pain, subsequent hypotension, and ECG findings of ST-segment elevation is consistent with acute coronary syndrome complicated by cardiogenic shock.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be overlooked if the initial vital signs are misleadingly normal, and the subsequent hypotension is attributed to other causes.

candidates.name: Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy
support_spans: sudden-onset chest pain
ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF
subsequent hypotension
contradict_spans: thrombotic occlusion of the distal left circumflex artery
candidates.why: The patient's presentation with sudden-onset chest pain, ECG findings of ST-segment elevation, and subsequent hypotension could be consistent with takotsubo cardiomyopathy, although the presence of thrombotic occlusion makes this less likely.
candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be overlooked if the focus is solely on the coronary occlusion, and the unique features of takotsubo cardiomyopathy are not considered.

candidates.protected_reason: This diagnosis may be overlooked if the focus is solely on the coronary occlusion and ECG findings, and the possibility of aortic dissection is not considered.
